description: This bar chart, from the paper “Breaking Bias, Building Bridges: Evaluation and Mitigation of Social Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis,” illustrates the change in bias percentage across three contact conditions—“Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact”—before and after exposure to different types of contact. The vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70, with tick marks at regular intervals. The horizontal axis lists the three contact conditions. For each condition, there are three stacked bars representing the bias percentage before contact (“No Contact Before,” “Positive Contact Before,” “Negative Contact Before”) and three corresponding bars representing the bias percentage after contact (“No Contact After,” “Positive Contact After,” “Negative Contact After”), each with a distinct color and pattern as indicated in the legend. The bars are grouped by condition and stacked to show the total bias percentage for each condition, with the individual components labeled with their respective values. For “Support of Authorities,” the bias percentages are 39.50% for “No Contact Before,” 31.83% for “Positive Contact Before,” and 42.38% for “Negative Contact Before,” all of which are shown as separate bars. For “Extended Contact,” the values are 40.61% for “No Contact Before,” 36.13% for “Positive Contact Before,” and 47.28% for “Negative Contact Before.” For “Virtual Contact,” the stacked bars show 39.74% for “No Contact Before,” 39.17% for “Positive Contact Before,” and 43.83% for “Negative Contact Before,” with the total bias percentage for each condition labeled at the top of the stacked bar. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color and pattern coding.
